decisions.reason: As a newly launched core drainage component with its own product page and strong fit to the firm's engineered system approach, its market potential is still unresolved and the option value likely exceeds near-term carrying cost.

A floor-level shower drainage system sits directly in the firm's strategic direction toward accessible, low-profile bathroom solutions, so management would likely wait for more market feedback rather than exit early.

Because this designer shower drainage line is presented as a flagship and closely matches the firm's design-conscious positioning, management would see high strategic option value and very little reason to withdraw it after only one year.
The integrated-slope shower element supports installation ease and system integration, making it a strategically coherent new option that is still too young for its uncertainty to have resolved.

Although somewhat more niche than the core shower offering, the backflow-protected basement drain has a dedicated launch message and clear functional value, so the firm would likely keep it while demand information develops.

The air-admittance valve appears less central to the firm's main bathroom-drainage focus and faces more internal competition for attention, but as a recent launch its value is still uncertain enough that management would more likely retain than drop it.
